title: Macroeconomics Adventure 2: Inflation & Unemployment
welcome_lead: Today you'll measure inflation with CPI and dissect unemployment by cause.
meta_desc: Economics Macro: CPI inflation, demand-pull, cost-push, and types of unemployment.
final_note: You measured CPI inflation and classified unemployment by cause.

walkthroughs.body_html:
The CPI tracks the cost of a fixed basket of goods.

Weighted by household spending; rebased to 100 in a chosen year.

Limits: ignores quality change, substitution bias, plutocratic weighting, omits owner-occupied housing in some countries.

Demand-pull: AD shifts right faster than AS — booming consumption, monetary expansion.

Cost-push: SRAS shifts left — oil shock, wage push, depreciation raises import costs.

Costs of inflation: menu costs, shoe-leather costs, redistribution from savers to borrowers, lost competitiveness.

Frictional — between jobs.

Structural — skills mismatch (coal miners after pit closure).

Cyclical (demand-deficient) — recession-driven.

Seasonal — tied to time of year.

Natural rate ≈ frictional + structural.

mcqs.q: What is the technical definition of a recession?
options: A recession is when prices fall and people lose jobs.
Revenue is profit before tax and profit is revenue after tax.
Two consecutive quarters of negative real GDP growth — a contraction of the economy.
A recession is when the stock market crashes.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between revenue and profit?
options: Revenue and profit mean the same thing.
A recession is when the stock market crashes.
Revenue is profit before tax and profit is revenue after tax.
Revenue is total income from sales (price x quantity); profit is what remains after deducting costs from revenue.
Revenue is profit before tax and profit is revenue after tax.
The change from one additional unit — marginal cost is the cost of producing one more unit; marginal utility is the satisfaction from one more unit. Marginal is incremental, not total or average.
Marginal cost is the total cost of producing all units.
Marginal means unimportant or small.
